copyPanel.rule: Graphing Inequalities on the Number Line
steps: 1. Draw the boundary circle at the given constant number

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Earning Money
revealWordProblem.text:
Yuzuki wants to earn enough money to go on a class trip that costs $750. The HelpingHand app shows the jobs she can take: $5 for dog walking, $20 for a car wash, and $25 for lawn mowing.
Question: What are some ways that Yuzuki can earn at least $750? Write an inequality for the amount she needs, and describe two different combinations of jobs that work.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A phone screen for the HelpingHand app listing jobs and pay: Dog Walking $5, Car Wash $20, Lawn Mowing $25.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Let m be the money Yuzuki earns. 'At least $750' means m ≥ 750, so on a number line the circle at 750 is closed and the shading goes right. Now find combinations that satisfy it. Lawn mowing only: 25n ≥ 750 gives n ≥ 30, so 30 lawns. Car washes only: 20n ≥ 750 gives n ≥ 37.5, so 38 washes. Mixed: 20 lawns and 10 car washes earns 20(25) + 10(20) = $700, which is not enough, so add 10 dog walks for $50 more and the total is $750 — exactly at the limit, which still counts because the inequality allows equality.

reviewHighlights.rule: Graphing Inequalities on the Number Line
steps: 1. Draw the boundary circle at the given constant number
2. Open Circle (○) for < or > (boundary value is not included in solution set)
3. Closed Circle (●) for ≤ or ≥ (boundary value is included). Shade right for >, left for <
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Graph Inequalities is treating ≥ and ≤ the same as > and < and drawing the wrong circle. For example, students often graph x ≥ 6 with an OPEN circle (as if it were x > 6), which wrongly excludes 6 even though 6 itself makes x ≥ 6 true. A second common mistake is choosing the right circle but shading the wrong direction — for x < 9 students sometimes shade right instead of left. Always check the symbol twice: once for the circle (does it have an 'or equal to' line?) and once for the shading direction (does the symbol point toward larger or smaller numbers?).

level3.stem: Clue: the witness ran more than 15 feet, so d > 15. On the number line, what do you draw?
level3.explanation: 'Greater than' (>) is a strict symbol, so 15 is NOT included — open circle. Larger values work, so shade right.
choiceFeedback: Your shading direction is right — the circle is the question. Does running EXACTLY 15 feet count as 'more than 15'? That decides open versus closed.
Shading left would mean distances under 15 feet count, but the witness ran farther than that. Test d = 10 in d > 15 to check.
This includes 15 and shades the shorter distances. Ask whether running exactly 15 feet fits "more than 15," then check the direction with a sample value.
level3.stemEs: Pista: el testigo corrió más de 15 pies, así que d > 15. En la recta numérica, ¿qué dibujas?
level3.explanationEs: "Mayor que" (>) es un símbolo estricto, así que 15 NO está incluido: círculo abierto. Los valores mayores sí funcionan, así que se sombrea hacia la derecha.
hints: The circle shows whether the boundary number itself counts as a solution, and the shading shows every other number that works.
Decide first whether running exactly 15 feet fits the phrase "more than 15 feet."
Try d = 20 in d > 15 and see whether it works, then try d = 10. The side that passes the test is the side you shade.
hintsEs: El círculo muestra si el número límite cuenta como solución, y el sombreado muestra todos los demás números que funcionan.
Primero decide si correr exactamente 15 pies cumple con la frase "más de 15 pies".
Prueba d = 20 en d > 15 y observa si funciona; después prueba d = 10. El lado que pasa la prueba es el lado que se sombrea.
choicesEs: Círculo abierto en 15, sombrea a la derecha
Círculo cerrado en 15, sombrea a la derecha
Círculo abierto en 15, sombrea a la izquierda
Círculo cerrado en 15, sombrea a la izquierda

level3.stem: Clue: the getaway car held at most 4 suspects, so s ≤ 4. How is this graphed?
level3.explanation: 'Less than or equal to' (≤) includes 4 — closed circle. Smaller values work, so shade left.
choiceFeedback: The direction is right. Now the circle: is exactly 4 suspects allowed by 'at most 4'? Answer that before choosing open or closed.
Shading right would allow more than 4 suspects, but "at most 4" caps the number. Test s = 6 in s ≤ 4 to see the problem.
This leaves 4 out and shades the larger numbers. Decide whether exactly 4 suspects is allowed by "at most 4," then re-check the direction.
level3.stemEs: Pista: el carro de escape llevaba como máximo 4 sospechosos, así que s ≤ 4. ¿Cómo se grafica esto?
level3.explanationEs: "Menor o igual que" (≤) incluye el 4: círculo cerrado. Los valores menores también funcionan, así que se sombrea hacia la izquierda.
hints: "At most" sets a ceiling — it names the largest value that is still allowed.
Decide whether exactly 4 suspects is permitted, since that choice sets the circle type.
Test s = 4 and then s = 2 in s ≤ 4. Both outcomes together tell you the circle and the shading direction.
hintsEs: "Como máximo" pone un tope: nombra el valor más grande que todavía se permite.
Decide si se permiten exactamente 4 sospechosos, porque esa decisión define el tipo de círculo.
Prueba s = 4 y luego s = 2 en s ≤ 4. Los dos resultados juntos te dicen el círculo y la dirección del sombreado.
choicesEs: Círculo cerrado en 4, sombrea a la izquierda
Círculo abierto en 4, sombrea a la izquierda
Círculo cerrado en 4, sombrea a la derecha
Círculo abierto en 4, sombrea a la derecha

level3.explanation: x < 5 means 5 is NOT included (open circle) and values less than 5 are shaded (left).
choiceFeedback: The direction is right, but < does not include 5, so the circle stays open.
This shades the values above 5. Test a number like 7 in x < 5 and see whether it belongs in the solution set.
This both fills in 5 and shades the larger side. Try x = 5 and x = 7 in the inequality — check whether either one makes it true.
hints: Every inequality graph asks two questions: is 5 itself a solution (circle type), and which side holds the solutions (shading)?
Strict symbols like < exclude the boundary, so check whether 5 makes x < 5 true. Then shade toward test values that work.
First step: 5 < 5 is false, so 5 is NOT included — that fixes the circle type. Now test x = 4 to find the shading direction.
level3.explanationEs: x < 5 significa que 5 NO está incluido (círculo abierto) y se sombrean los valores menores que 5 (hacia la izquierda).
choicesEs: Círculo abierto en 5, sombreado a la izquierda
Círculo cerrado en 5, sombreado a la izquierda
Círculo abierto en 5, sombreado a la derecha
Círculo cerrado en 5, sombreado a la derecha
hintsEs: Toda gráfica de desigualdad hace dos preguntas: ¿es 5 mismo una solución (tipo de círculo) y de qué lado están las soluciones (sombreado)?
Los símbolos estrictos como < excluyen el límite, así que revisa si 5 hace verdadera x < 5. Luego sombrea hacia los valores de prueba que sí funcionan.
Primer paso: 5 < 5 es falso, así que 5 NO se incluye; eso fija el tipo de círculo. Ahora prueba x = 4 para hallar la dirección del sombreado.

level3.explanation: x ≥ 3 means 3 IS included (closed circle) and values greater than or equal to 3 are shaded (right).
choiceFeedback: The direction is right, but ≥ includes 3, so the circle should be filled in.
This shades the numbers below 3. Test x = 1 in x ≥ 3 to see whether small values satisfy the inequality.
This leaves 3 out and shades the smaller side. Check whether x = 3 makes x ≥ 3 true, and test x = 1 as well.
hints: Check the symbol: ≥ has the 'or equal' bar. What does that bar mean for the circle at 3?
The bar means 3 IS a solution, so the circle gets filled in. Then a quick test value tells you the shading side.
First step: 3 ≥ 3 is true, so 3 is included. Now test x = 10 — is 10 ≥ 3 true? Shade toward that side.
level3.explanationEs: x ≥ 3 significa que 3 SÍ está incluido (círculo cerrado) y se sombrean los valores mayores o iguales que 3 (hacia la derecha).
choicesEs: Círculo cerrado en 3, sombreado a la derecha
Círculo abierto en 3, sombreado a la derecha
Círculo cerrado en 3, sombreado a la izquierda
Círculo abierto en 3, sombreado a la izquierda
hintsEs: Revisa el símbolo: ≥ tiene la barra de 'o igual'. ¿Qué significa esa barra para el círculo en el 3?
La barra significa que 3 SÍ es solución, así que el círculo se rellena. Luego un valor de prueba te dice el lado del sombreado.
Primer paso: 3 ≥ 3 es verdadero, así que el 3 se incluye. Ahora prueba x = 10: ¿es 10 ≥ 3 verdadero? Sombrea hacia ese lado.

level3.explanation: x > 8 means 8 is NOT included (open circle) and values greater than 8 are shaded to the right.
choiceFeedback: The direction is right, but > does not include 8, so the circle stays open.
This shades the values below 8. Substitute x = 4 into x > 8 and check whether it works.
This fills in 8 and shades the smaller side. Try x = 8 and x = 4 in x > 8 and see whether either one belongs.
hints: Two decisions: does x = 8 make x > 8 true, and are the solutions bigger or smaller than 8?
Symbols without the 'or equal' bar exclude the boundary. Then shade only the side where test numbers make the statement true.
First step: 8 > 8 is false, so 8 is NOT included — that fixes your circle. Now test x = 9 to pick the shading side.
level3.explanationEs: x > 8 significa que 8 NO está incluido (círculo abierto) y se sombrean los valores mayores que 8 (hacia la derecha).
choicesEs: Círculo abierto en 8, sombreado a la derecha
Círculo cerrado en 8, sombreado a la derecha
Círculo abierto en 8, sombreado a la izquierda
Círculo cerrado en 8, sombreado a la izquierda
hintsEs: Dos decisiones: ¿hace x = 8 verdadera x > 8, y las soluciones son mayores o menores que 8?
Los símbolos sin la barra de 'o igual' excluyen el límite. Luego sombrea solo el lado donde los números de prueba hacen verdadero el enunciado.
Primer paso: 8 > 8 es falso, así que el 8 NO se incluye; eso fija tu círculo. Ahora prueba x = 9 para elegir el lado del sombreado.
